learn.title: Solar PV Electricity via Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar PV panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect, a cornerstone technology for decarbonizing power generation. Understanding this process highlights how sunlight becomes clean energy without moving parts or emissions, making it vital for India's 90 GW solar target by 2030.
learn.c1_text: When photons strike a semiconductor material like silicon, they knock electrons loose, creating electric current. Like marbles rolling off a table when pushed, photons transfer energy to electrons, freeing them to flow as electricity in a circuit.
learn.c2_text: Silicon cells have a p-n junction with positive and negative layers. Sunlight hitting the junction creates electron-hole pairs. Metal contacts collect these electrons, forming DC current. A typical 1m² panel generates 150-200W, enough for 10 LED bulbs.
learn.c3_text: India's solar capacity reached 60 GW in 2023, with 10 GW added in one year. Projects like Bhadla Solar Park (2.25 GW) demonstrate scale. The National Solar Mission aims for 100 GW hybrid renewable capacity by 2030.

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes, enabling scalable grid storage for renewable energy. Their long lifespan and rapid scaling potential address intermittency challenges, crucial for India's 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030.
learn.c1_text: Vanadium ions in different oxidation states flow through membranes, creating current during redox reactions. Like a liquid battery, capacity scales with tank size. Vanadium systems offer 15,000+ charge cycles and 20-year lifespan.
learn.c2_text: Iron electrolytes use cheaper materials, with ferrous/ferric ions exchanging electrons. These systems achieve 70-85% efficiency and 10-hour discharge duration. Cost is 30% lower than lithium-ion, ideal for grid backup.
learn.c3_text: India's 2023 Energy Storage Mission targets 500 MWh deployment. Projects like Kurnool 100 MW/200 MWh vanadium flow battery showcase commercial viability. The ministry aims for 10 GWh storage by 2030.
learn.stat4: Flow battery costs: 30% lower than Li-ion

learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar parks on reservoirs and lakes reduce land use while enhancing water conservation through reduced evaporation. With India's 160 GW renewable target, these systems offer dual benefits of clean energy and water preservation in water-stressed regions.
learn.c1_text: Floating PV uses 90% less land than ground-mounted systems. Like a solar-powered lid, panels reduce water evaporation by 30-50%. The 5 MW Kerala floating plant generates 7.5 million kWh/year while conserving 2.5 million liters daily.
learn.c2_text: Cooler panel temperatures improve efficiency by 5-10%. Evaporation reduction saves water in drought-prone areas. A 100 MW floating plant can conserve 200 million liters annually. Iran's 2 MW floating plant achieved 20% higher output than land-based systems.
learn.c3_text: India's National Institute of Wind Energy installed 100 kW in Tamil Nadu. Gujarat's 5 MW plant on Sardar Sarovar Dam demonstrates scale. The ministry targets 40 GW floating solar by 2030, focusing on reservoirs and canal top installations.

learn.title: Wind Turbine Lifespan & Recycling
learn.intro: Wind turbine blades require innovative recycling solutions as they reach end-of-life. With India's 60 GW wind capacity, managing 100,000+ tons of composite blade waste annually demands circular economy approaches to sustain the sector's growth trajectory.
learn.c1_text: Modern turbines operate 25-30 years with 3% annual maintenance. Gearbox failures cause 50% of downtime. Condition monitoring systems predict issues, reducing O&M costs by 20%. Offshore turbines need specialized corrosion-resistant materials.
learn.c2_text: Fiberglass/epoxy blades take centuries to decompose. Mechanical recycling crushes into granules for cement production. Chemical processes break resins for new composites. Sweden's 2023 pilot plant converts blades to building materials, achieving 90% reuse rate.
learn.c3_text: India's 2023 Windblade Recycling Scheme partners with startups. Gujarat's 100-ton facility converts blades to construction materials. The ministry mandates 15% recycled content in new turbines from 2025, aligning with 100 GW wind target.
learn.stat3: Recycling reduces CO2 by 15% vs virgin materials

learn.title: Green Hydrogen via Water Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen production through water electrolysis decarbonizes heavy industry and transport. With India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targeting 5 MT/year production, understanding PEM vs alkaline electrolyzers is key to scaling this clean fuel solution.
learn.c1_text: Proton exchange membranes use platinum catalysts for rapid reactions at 80°C. Flexible operation responds to renewable intermittency. Efficiency reaches 70-80%. Siemens' 10 MW German plant produces 1.2 tons/day hydrogen for steelmaking.
learn.c2_text: Alkaline electrolyzers use potassium hydroxide and nickel electrodes, operating at 70-90°C. Lower capex ($300-500/kW) but slower response. Efficiency 65-75%. FuelCell Energy's 200 MW plant in Ohio supplies 40,000 tons/year for ammonia production.
learn.c3_text: India's 2023 mission aims for 5 MT green H2 by 2030 with 127 GW renewable capacity. Projects like Adani's $8.5B green H2 complex in Tamil Nadu will produce 1 million tons/year by 2030, targeting steel and fertilizer sectors.

learn.title: Concentrated Solar Power Systems
learn.intro: Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) uses mirrors to focus sunlight, generating electricity with thermal storage capabilities. As India integrates 500 GW renewables, CSP's 8-hour storage potential offers grid stability solutions, especially in sunny desert regions like Rajasthan.
learn.c1_text: Parabolic troughs or power towers use heliostats to focus light onto receivers. Like magnifying glass focusing sunlight, 500x concentration heats oil to 400°C. Kamuthi CSP in Tamil Nadu uses 25,000 heliostats to generate 64 MW continuously.
learn.c2_text: Molten salt (600°C) stores heat for 8-10 hours, enabling night power. Like a thermal battery, this allows 24/7 operation. Spain's Gemasolar plant achieved 100% solar steam generation. CSP reduces curtailment by 30% vs PV in arid zones.
learn.c3_text: India's 500 MW CSP capacity spans Rajasthan and Gujarat. The 100 MW Kurnool CSP plant uses 12-hour storage. The ministry targets 20 GW CSP by 2030, focusing on desert regions with 2,800+ kWh/m² solar insolation. New projects integrate with green hydrogen production.
